Capital Improvements
None are planned; no impact.
Community Facilities
The Mayfair Community Center is located in an area of high liquefaction potential and high to moderately high vertical and lateral ground failure potential. The CDBG plan for this Center is to expand the building by approximately 1,000 square feet. This expansion should be done in conformance with the Uniform Building Code and policies in the San Jose seismic safety element of the General Plan.
Northside CNRA:
Housing Rehabilitation
The CDBG program plans to make funds available for the rehabilitation of 101 residences in this neighborhood. To the extent that these monies are used to identify and rectify structural problems relating to seismic stability, the environment impact will be positive. The foregoing discussion concerning seismic risk and older dwellings (refer to section on Gardner CNRA) is also relevant to the Northside community.
Capital Improvements
The replacement of old and deteriorated curbs and sidewalks in this area may be affected by a future seismic event. The geologic and soils conditions in the Northside area are such that sidewalks and curbs may be adversely impacted by small localized ground failures and soil movements.
Community Facilities
The proposed improvements to Backesto Park include the construction of a shelter-type recreation building. The potential geologic impact is minimal. The park is located in an area of high liquefaction potential and moderately weak and expansive soils. There exists a very slight possibility of soil movements which would adversely affect the planned tennis courts.
The Northside Community Center was constructed as part of the previous threeyear CDBG program and received environmental review and approval at that time. The current plan proposes very minor improvements which will entail no adverse geologic impact.
The Nihonmachi Community Services Program is an on-going public service which does not involve CDBG funding in any structure; hence, no geologic impact.
